text.p: Here is how major stock markets outside the United States ended on Wednesday.

LONDON - A weak opening on Wall Street and worries about higher U.S. and UK interest rates dragged the UK stock market down on Wednesday. The FTSE 100 share index closed a lacklustre trading session 16.6 points lower at 3,955.7, just off the day's lows. The Dow Jones Industrial Average was down eight points at the time.

FRANKFURT - German shares eased slightly in bourse trade on Wednesday, their pace checked a bit by overnight weakness on Wall Street, but they were still resilient after the recent run-up to record levels. The 30-share DAX index ended down 2.38 points at 2,625.70 after hovering in a six-point range throughout the session. In post-bourse trade the index stood at 2,621.20 down 5.23.

PARIS - The French stockmarket showed little reaction to the French 1997 budget unveiled on Wednesday and closed slightly lower as it digested recent gains. "The market is consolidating calmly. The budget conformed to expectations," a trader said. The blue-chip CAC-40 index closed down 8.13 points or 0.39 percent at 2,072.73.

ZURICH - Swiss shares ended a volatile day virtually unchanged while investors concentrated on banking group Swiss Bank Corp (SBC). SBC added 4.75 francs, or 2.01 percent, to end at 241.50 after announcing a restructuring of its domestic operations. The measures include 1,700 job cuts, write-offs totalling 3.3 billion francs. SBC also forecast of a 1996 loss of 1.9 billion francs. The all-share Swiss Performance Index lost 1.25 points, or 0.05 percent, to end at 2,365.47.

TOKYO - Tokyo stocks were dealt a setback on Wednesday as profit-talking emerged to send the key Nikkei average down after big gains over the last two trading days. But brokers said that the index is likely to be supported at around 21,000 where investors' buying is said to be positioned. The key Nikkei 225 average closed down 153.84 points at 21,156.75.

HONG KONG - Hong Kong's Hang Seng Index closed modestly easier on Wednesday, off lows but just below its important resistance level of 11,600, as profit-takers and bulls struggled to dictate the market's direction, brokers said. The Hang Seng Index closed down 27.58 points at 11,594.03 after trending as much as 95 points down during the day.

SYDNEY - The Australian share market slipped further in late trading on Wednesday on continuing concerns about the direction of metal prices and emerging bearish sentiment towards industrial shares. The All Ordinaries index closed 19.30 points lower at 2235.10.

JOHANNESBURG - South African shares' run-up of the past two days was halted on Wednesday with stocks toppling off their high levels on profit-taking and as futures baskets were unwound. The industrial index lost 56.5 points to 8,155.2 dragging down the the overall index 36 points to 6,911.1. Gold shares took a knock, uninspired by bullion's hold on the $383 level, dealers said. The gold index ended 20.2 points or over one percent weaker at 1,756.3.
